title: Reading the Value of the Items on a Catalogue Order Against the Card
content:
Where a catalogue order against a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card is stopped, what the items themselves came to is read from the order's own record where that record shows it, from the card where it does not, and from the card's tier where neither shows it.

The value of the items is the total the order's own record shows the items came to, where an order stands on the card and its record shows that total; it is what the catalogue took off the card less the delivery charge the order carried, where an order stands whose record does not show that total but the card shows a transaction made through the catalogue for it; and it is the smallest order the card's tier will process in every other case.

**Where each figure is found.** An order stands where it is recorded against the programme as placed. The total the items came to is the order total carried on that order's own record, taken from the most recent standing order by the day it was placed. What the catalogue took off the card is the total of the settled card transactions made through the catalogue. The smallest order the card's tier will process is the catalogue order minimum that tier carries.

**Input, judgement, result.**

- *Input:* an order stands and its record shows a total of 46.50 USD. *Result:* the value of the items is 46.50 USD.
- *Input:* an order stands, its record shows no total, and the card shows catalogue transactions of 52.45 USD settled, the order having carried a delivery charge of 5.95 USD. *Result:* the value of the items is 46.50 USD.
- *Input:* no order stands, on a card whose tier will process orders of no less than 10.00 USD. *Result:* the value of the items is 10.00 USD.

The second figure is never taken below nothing: where the delivery charge exceeds what the catalogue took off the card, the value of the items is nothing.
